# vela

> A WebGPU-first 3D rendering engine written from scratch in TypeScript — built to explore what a modern engine looks like without the weight of legacy WebGL paths or old-browser support. PBR shading, a glTF loader, and an interactive viewer in ~3k lines.

vela is a WebGPU-only 3D rendering engine designed for AI agents building games:
declarative APIs, no hidden update flags, actionable error messages, deterministic
rendering, pixel readback, and built-in scene diagnostics. TypeScript, zero runtime
dependencies.

Quick start:

```ts
import { WebGPURenderer, Scene, PerspectiveCamera, Mesh, BoxGeometry,
         StandardMaterial, DirectionalLight, Vector3 } from 'vela';

const renderer = new WebGPURenderer({ canvas });
await renderer.init();
const scene = new Scene();
scene.sky = { sunDirection: new Vector3(0.4, 0.7, 0.2) };  // procedural daylight + IBL
scene.skybox = true;
scene.add(new Mesh(new BoxGeometry(), new StandardMaterial({ color: 0x6699ff })));
const light = new DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 3);
scene.add(light, light.target);
const camera = new PerspectiveCamera(45, canvas.width / canvas.height, 0.1, 100);
camera.position.set(3, 2, 5); camera.lookAt(new Vector3(0, 0, 0));
function frame() { requestAnimationFrame(frame); renderer.render(scene, camera); }
frame();
```

Stuck? `renderer.diagnose(scene, camera)` explains black screens with fixes;
`describeScene(scene, camera)` and `renderer.report()` return JSON state;
`await renderer.screenshot()` shows you the frame; `expectFrame(...)` turns
visuals into assertions. Docs: docs/GETTING_STARTED.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md,
docs/SHADER_MATERIAL.md, ROADMAP.md.

## Classes

### class Object3D
Base node of the scene graph: a transform with a parent and children.
- id: string
- isObject3D: true
- name: string
- type: string
- parent: Object3D | null
- children: Object3D[]
- position: Vector3
- rotation: Euler
- quaternion: Quaternion
- scale: Vector3
- matrix: Matrix4
- matrixWorld: Matrix4
- matrixAutoUpdate: boolean — When true, local matrix is recomposed from position/quaternion/scale each update.
- matrixWorldNeedsUpdate: boolean
- visible: boolean
- frustumCulled: boolean — When true, the renderer may skip this object if its bounds are off-screen.
- add(objects: Object3D[]): Object3D
- remove(objects: Object3D[]): Object3D
- removeFromParent(): Object3D
- traverse(callback: (object: Object3D) => void): void — Depth-first traversal including self.
- traverseVisible(callback: (object: Object3D) => void): void
- getWorldPosition(target: Vector3): Vector3
- lookAt(x: number | Vector3, y?: number | undefined, z?: number | undefined): void — Orient this object so its -Z axis points toward the target (world space).
- up: Vector3
- updateMatrix(): void
- updateMatrixWorld(force?: boolean): void — Recompute world matrices for this subtree.
- updateWorldMatrix(updateParents: boolean, updateChildren: boolean): void — Update world matrix of this node, optionally walking up parents and/or down children.

### class Raycaster
Picks meshes along a ray. A bounding-sphere test rejects far-away meshes cheaply; survivors are tested per-triangle in the mesh's local space, so hits carry an exact point, the triangle index, and an interpolated UV.
- ray: Ray
- near: number
- far: number
- precise: boolean — When false, the per-triangle pass is skipped and meshes are picked at the bounding-sphere level (faster, coarser).
- bvhThreshold: number — Triangle count at or above which a cached BVH accelerates the precise pass instead of a linear scan.
- setFromCamera(ndcX: number, ndcY: number, camera: Camera): Raycaster — Build the ray from normalized device coords (x, y in [-1, 1]).
- intersect(root: Object3D, recursive?: boolean): Intersection[] — Intersect a subtree; returns hits sorted nearest-first.

### class BVH
A median-split bounding-volume hierarchy over a geometry's triangles, used to skip the per-triangle linear scan when raycasting dense meshes. Built once and cached on the geometry; traversal prunes subtrees whose AABB the ray misses.
- new BVH(triangles: Uint32Array<ArrayBufferLike>, root: BVHNode)
- triangles: Uint32Array<ArrayBufferLike> — Triangle indices in leaf order (triangle `t` spans vertices 3t..3t+2).
- intersect(ray: Ray, visit: (triangleIndex: number) => void): void — Visit every triangle whose leaf AABB the ray may cross.

### class Scene extends Object3D
Root of a renderable scene graph, with optional background and ambient fill.
- isScene: true
- background: Color | null
- ambientColor: Color — Flat ambient irradiance applied to all PBR materials.
- ambientIntensity: number
- environment: Texture | null — Equirectangular environment map for image-based lighting.
- environmentIntensity: number — Multiplier on the environment's contribution.
- sky: SkyOptions | null — Procedural daylight sky.
- skybox: boolean — Draw the environment (or procedural sky) as the background.
- fog: FogOptions | null — Distance fog applied to all lit materials (PBR and ShaderMaterial).
- backgroundBlur: number — Blur the skybox background: 0 = sharp, 1 = fully blurred (mip-based).

### class Camera extends Object3D
Base camera: holds projection and the inverse-world (view) matrix.
- isCamera: true
- projectionMatrix: Matrix4
- projectionMatrixInverse: Matrix4
- matrixWorldInverse: Matrix4 — View matrix = inverse(world matrix).
- updateMatrixWorld(force?: boolean | undefined): void — Recompute world matrices for this subtree.
- updateWorldMatrix(updateParents: boolean, updateChildren: boolean): void — Update world matrix of this node, optionally walking up parents and/or down children.

### class PerspectiveCamera extends Camera
- new PerspectiveCamera(fov: number, aspect: number, near: number, far: number)
- isPerspectiveCamera: true
- fov: number — Vertical field of view in degrees.
- aspect: number
- near: number
- far: number
- updateProjectionMatrix(): void

### class OrthographicCamera extends Camera
Orthographic projection camera (no perspective foreshortening). Useful for CAD-style views, 2D overlays, and shadow-map light cameras.
- new OrthographicCamera(left: number, right: number, top: number, bottom: number, near: number, far: number)
- isOrthographicCamera: true
- left: number
- right: number
- top: number
- bottom: number
- near: number
- far: number
- zoom: number — Uniform scale on the frustum half-extents.
- updateProjectionMatrix(): void

### class Mesh extends Object3D
A renderable: geometry paired with one (or more) materials.
- new Mesh(geometry: BufferGeometry, material: Material | Material[])
- isMesh: true
- geometry: BufferGeometry
- material: Material | Material[]
- shell: Shell | null — Optional inverted-hull overlay draw (outlines, fur, highlights).
- morphTargetInfluences: number[] — Per-morph-target blend weights, parallel to `geometry.morphAttributes.position`.
- morphTargetDictionary: Record<string, number> | null — Optional name → target-index map (from glTF `mesh.extras.targetNames`).

### class LineSegments extends Mesh
A set of disconnected line segments: the position attribute is read in pairs (0-1, 2-3, …) and drawn with `line-list` topology. Reuses the scene-graph and culling machinery of {@link Mesh}; the renderer routes it to the line pipeline.
- new LineSegments(geometry: BufferGeometry, material: LineBasicMaterial)
- isLineSegments: true

### class SkinnedMesh extends Mesh
A mesh deformed on the GPU by a skeleton. The geometry must carry `joints` (vec4 uint) and `weights` (vec4 float) attributes; the renderer uploads the skeleton's bone matrices and uses the skinned pipeline variant.
- new SkinnedMesh(geometry: BufferGeometry, material: Material | Material[], skeleton: Skeleton)
- isSkinnedMesh: true
- skeleton: Skeleton

### class InstancedMesh extends Mesh
Renders one geometry many times in a single draw call. Each instance has its own model matrix stored in `instanceMatrix` (16 floats per instance); the renderer uploads them to a storage buffer read by the instanced vertex shader.
- new InstancedMesh(geometry: BufferGeometry, material: Material | Material[], count: number)
- isInstancedMesh: true
- count: number
- instanceMatrix: Float32Array<ArrayBuffer>
- version: number — Bump (or call `needsUpdate`) after editing matrices to re-upload.
- setMatrixAt(index: number, matrix: Matrix4): void
- getMatrixAt(index: number, target: Matrix4): void
- needsUpdate(): void

### class ParticleSystem extends Object3D
A GPU-simulated particle emitter: a compute pass integrates a fixed-capacity pool (positions/velocities/age live only on the GPU; the hot path allocates nothing per particle), and one instanced draw renders camera-facing soft discs. Emission happens at this object's world position — move it like any Object3D to make trails.
- new ParticleSystem(options: ParticleSystemOptions)
- isParticleSystem: true
- options: ParticleSystemOptions
- emitting: boolean — Pause emission (existing particles keep simulating).

### class TrailRenderer extends Mesh
A ribbon that trails an object's motion: each `update(cameraPosition)` samples `target`'s world position into a fixed-capacity history and rebuilds a camera-facing triangle strip through it (world space — keep the trail itself at the scene root). Reuses the standard mesh path, so any `Material` works; drive it from your loop like `controls.update()`. Geometry is offline-verifiable.
- new TrailRenderer(options: TrailOptions)
- isTrail: true
- target: Object3D — Emitter sampled each update.
- maxPoints: number
- width: number
- widthTail: number
- minDistance: number
- reset(): void — Clear the history (the ribbon disappears until points accumulate again).
- update(cameraPosition: Vector3): void — Sample `target`, append a point if it moved far enough, and rebuild the ribbon.

### class Sprite extends Object3D
A camera-facing textured quad. World-space by default (sized in world units, depth-tested against the scene — labels, pickups, billboards); set `screenSpace = true` for HUD elements sized in CSS pixels and drawn on top of everything.
- new Sprite(texture: Texture | null)
- isSprite: true
- texture: Texture | null — Color texture (un-set = solid `color` quad).
- color: Color — Tint multiplied with the texture.
- opacity: number
- size: Vector2 — Quad size: world units, or CSS pixels when `screenSpace`.
- offset: Vector2 — Extra offset from the anchor point, in the same units as `size` (x right, y up).
- screenSpace: boolean — Draw as a HUD overlay: no depth test, sized in CSS pixels.

### class LOD extends Object3D
Level-of-detail node: shows one of several child representations based on distance to the camera, so distant objects render cheaper geometry. Add levels nearest-first; the renderer calls `update()` each frame (when `autoUpdate`) to pick the active level by toggling child visibility, so LOD composes with frustum culling and every other traversal for free.
- isLOD: true
- levels: Level[]
- autoUpdate: boolean — Let the renderer pick the level each frame.
- addLevel(object: Object3D, distance?: number, hysteresis?: number): LOD — Add a level shown at/beyond `distance` (world units).
- update(cameraPosition: Vector3): void — Select the active level for `cameraPosition`, toggling child visibility.
- activeLevel: Object3D | null — The currently active level's object, or null.

### class TextMesh extends Object3D
Billboarded SDF text. Glyphs rasterize lazily into a per-font distance-field atlas and render through the sprite batcher — one instanced draw per font — so text stays crisp at any scale and cheap at any count. Supports `\n` for multiple lines. Mutate `text` (or any option) freely; everything re-reads each frame.
- new TextMesh(text: string, options: TextMeshOptions)
- isTextMesh: true
- text: string
- font: string
- fontSize: number
- color: Color
- opacity: number
- screenSpace: boolean
- anchor: "left" | "center" | "right"

### class RenderTarget
An offscreen render destination: `renderer.render(scene, camera, rt)` draws into it, and `rt.texture` works anywhere a sampled texture does — mirrors, portals, minimaps, security monitors:
- new RenderTarget(width: number, height: number)
- isRenderTarget: true
- width: number
- height: number
- texture: Texture — Sample this in any material (`map`, sprite texture, ...).

### class ReflectionProbe extends Object3D
A local reflection capture. Add it to a Scene; the renderer refreshes it automatically. The first four visible probes participate in nearest-two blending.
- new ReflectionProbe(options: ReflectionProbeOptions)
- isReflectionProbe: true
- resolution: number
- camera: PerspectiveCamera
- targets: readonly RenderTarget[]
- radius: number
- intensity: number
- refresh: ReflectionProbeRefresh
- refreshInterval: number
- needsUpdate: boolean — Set true after moving a static probe to request another capture.

### class IrradianceProbeGrid extends Object3D
A world-axis-aligned regular grid of baked diffuse-irradiance probes represented as SH-L2 coefficients. `position` is its minimum corner; rotation/scale are ignored.
- new IrradianceProbeGrid(options: IrradianceProbeGridOptions)
- isIrradianceProbeGrid: true
- dimensions: [number, number, number]
- spacing: Vector3
- coefficients: Float32Array<ArrayBuffer> | null — Nine RGB SH coefficients per probe, x-fastest; null until baked or restored.
- version: number
- probeCount: number
- setCoefficients(coefficients: Float32Array<ArrayBuffer>): IrradianceProbeGrid

### class Skeleton
A set of joint nodes plus their inverse bind matrices. Each frame `update()` recomputes `boneMatrices[i] = jointWorld[i] * inverseBind[i]` (already in world space), which the skinned vertex shader blends by vertex weights.
- new Skeleton(joints: Object3D[], boneInverses: Matrix4[])
- joints: Object3D[]
- boneInverses: Matrix4[]
- boneMatrices: Float32Array<ArrayBuffer> — Flat 16-floats-per-joint buffer uploaded to the GPU.
- jointCount: number
- update(): void — Recompute bone matrices from the joints' current world transforms.

### class BufferGeometry
Holds vertex attributes and an optional index buffer for a mesh.
- id: string
- isBufferGeometry: true
- name: string
- attributes: Record<string, BufferAttribute>
- index: BufferAttribute | null
- morphAttributes: { position?: BufferAttribute[] | undefined; normal?: BufferAttribute[] | undefined; } — Morph-target deltas.
- boundingBox: Box3 | null
- boundingSphere: Sphere | null
- version: number — Incremented when buffers are structurally replaced (forces GPU re-create).
- setAttribute(name: string, attribute: BufferAttribute): BufferGeometry
- getAttribute(name: string): BufferAttribute | undefined
- setIndex(index: BufferAttribute | TypedArray): BufferGeometry
- getDrawCount(): number — Number of vertices to draw (index count if indexed, else position count).
- computeBoundingBox(): void
- computeBoundingSphere(): void
- computeVertexNormals(): void — Generate smooth vertex normals from positions (indexed or non-indexed).

### class BufferAttribute
A view over interleaved or tightly-packed vertex data for one attribute.
- new BufferAttribute(array: TypedArray, itemSize: number, normalized: boolean)
- array: TypedArray
- itemSize: number
- normalized: boolean
- version: number — Bumped when the data changes so the renderer can re-upload.
- count: number
- getX(i: number): number
- getY(i: number): number
- getZ(i: number): number
- needsUpdate(): void

### class BoxGeometry extends BufferGeometry
A box centered at the origin.
- new BoxGeometry(width: number, height: number, depth: number)

### class SphereGeometry extends BufferGeometry
A UV sphere centered at the origin.
- new SphereGeometry(radius: number, widthSegments: number, heightSegments: number)

### class PlaneGeometry extends BufferGeometry
A flat plane on the XZ axes (normal +Y), centered at the origin.
- new PlaneGeometry(width: number, depth: number)

### class Material
Base material: render-state common to all shading models.
- id: string
- isMaterial: true
- name: string
- type: string
- side: Side
- transparent: boolean
- blending: Blending
- opacity: number
- depthTest: boolean
- depthWrite: boolean
- alphaTest: number — Alpha test cutoff; 0 disables.
- needsPipelineRebuild: boolean — Identifies the pipeline variant.

### class StandardMaterial extends Material
Physically based metallic-roughness material (glTF 2.0 compatible). Cook-Torrance GGX specular + Lambertian diffuse, evaluated in the renderer's WGSL PBR shader.
- new StandardMaterial(params: StandardMaterialParams)
- type: "StandardMaterial"
- color: Color
- metalness: number
- roughness: number
- emissive: Color
- emissiveIntensity: number
- normalScale: number
- occlusionStrength: number
- clearcoat: number — Clear-coat layer (KHR_materials_clearcoat): a thin dielectric specular coat.
- clearcoatRoughness: number
- ior: number — Index of refraction (KHR_materials_ior); 1.5 → the default 0.04 dielectric F0.
- specularIntensity: number — Dielectric specular strength and tint (KHR_materials_specular).
- specularColor: Color
- sheenColor: Color — Sheen layer (KHR_materials_sheen): a cloth-like retroreflective lobe.
- sheenRoughness: number
- transmission: number — Transmission factor (KHR_materials_transmission): glass-like refraction.
- thickness: number — Volume thickness (KHR_materials_volume); 0 = thin-walled.
- attenuationDistance: number — Distance light travels before attenuating to `attenuationColor`; 0 = none.
- attenuationColor: Color
- map: Texture | null
- normalMap: Texture | null
- metalnessRoughnessMap: Texture | null — glTF packs metalness in B, roughness in G.
- emissiveMap: Texture | null
- occlusionMap: Texture | null
- clearcoatMap: Texture | null — Per-texel clearcoat factor (R channel).
- clearcoatRoughnessMap: Texture | null — Per-texel clearcoat roughness (G channel).
- getFeatureKey(): number — Bitmask describing which texture maps are present (drives shader variants).

### class LineBasicMaterial extends Material
Unlit line material: a flat color (optionally modulated by per-vertex colors), evaluated in the renderer's WGSL line shader. Used by the debug helpers.
- new LineBasicMaterial(params: LineBasicMaterialParams)
- type: "LineBasicMaterial"
- color: Color
- vertexColors: boolean

### class ShaderMaterial extends Material
A custom-surface material: you write one WGSL function that produces PBR surface inputs (albedo, roughness, emissive, normal, ...) and the engine supplies everything else — all light types, shadows, IBL, clustered lighting, OIT, post-processing and tonemapping behave exactly as they do for StandardMaterial.
- new ShaderMaterial(options: ShaderMaterialOptions)
- isShaderMaterial: true
- type: "ShaderMaterial"
- uniforms: Record<string, UniformValue> — Custom uniform values; mutate freely (uploaded every frame).
- version: number — Bumped by setSurface(); part of the pipeline cache key.
- surfaceCode: string
- vertexCode: string | null
- lightCode: string | null
- ambientCode: string | null
- setSurface(code: string): void — Replace the surface function; the shader recompiles on next draw.
- setVertex(code: string | null): void — Set/replace/clear the vertex displacement function; recompiles on next draw.
- setLight(code: string | null): void — Set/replace/clear the per-light function; recompiles on next draw.
- setAmbient(code: string | null): void — Set/replace/clear the indirect-light function; recompiles on next draw.

### class ShaderPass
A custom fullscreen post-processing effect. Push instances into `renderer.passes`; they run in order in HDR linear space after the scene (and bloom/SSAO/TAA) and before tonemap, each reading the previous stage's color plus the scene depth.
- new ShaderPass(options: ShaderPassOptions)
- isShaderPass: true
- enabled: boolean
- name: string
- uniforms: Record<string, UniformValue>
- inputs: ShaderPassInput[] — Additional scene buffers this pass needs.
- version: number — Bumped by `setEffect()`; part of the pipeline cache key.
- id: string — Stable id for caching GPU resources.
- effectCode: string
- setEffect(code: string): void — Replace the effect function; recompiles on the next frame.

### class ComputeTask
A declarative GPU compute job: WGSL plus named storage/uniform buffers, with auto-built bind group layout and uniform packing — no raw WebGPU plumbing. Run it standalone (`await task.run()`) or fold it into a frame by passing the frame's encoder. Read storage results back with `task.read(name)` (requires `readable: true`).
- new ComputeTask(options: ComputeTaskOptions)
- name: string
- init(device: GPUDevice): Promise<void> — Create GPU resources on `device`.
- updateUniform(name: string, values: Record<string, UniformValue>): void — Re-pack and upload a uniform binding's values (call after mutating them).
- write(name: string, data: ArrayBufferView<ArrayBuffer>, offset?: number): void — Overwrite a storage buffer's contents (offset in bytes).
- dispatch(encoder?: GPUCommandEncoder | undefined, workgroups?: [number, (number | undefined)?, (number | undefined)?] | undefined): void — Encode the dispatch.
- run(workgroups?: [number, (number | undefined)?, (number | undefined)?] | undefined): void — Convenience: dispatch standalone.
- read(name: string): Promise<ArrayBuffer> — Read a `readable` storage buffer back to the CPU (resolves after the GPU finishes).
- buffer(name: string): GPUBuffer — Raw GPU buffer for a binding (e.g.
- dispose(): void — Release all GPU buffers.

### class GridHelper extends LineSegments
A wireframe grid on the XZ plane, centered at the origin. The two center lines (the X and Z axes) use `centerColor`; the rest use `gridColor`.
- new GridHelper(size: number, divisions: number, centerColor: ColorInput, gridColor: ColorInput)

### class AxesHelper extends LineSegments
Three lines from the origin: +X red, +Y green, +Z blue.
- new AxesHelper(size: number)

### class Box3Helper extends LineSegments
A wireframe box outlining a {@link Box3}; call {@link update} to re-fit.
- new Box3Helper(box: Box3, color: ColorInput)
- update(box: Box3): void — Rebuild the edge positions from `box` (in the box's own coordinate space).

### class DirectionalLightHelper extends LineSegments
A square at the light's position plus a line pointing toward its target. Add it to the scene root and call {@link update} each frame to track the light.
- new DirectionalLightHelper(light: DirectionalLight, size: number, color: ColorInput | undefined)
- light: DirectionalLight
- update(): void — Re-position/orient the gizmo from the light's current transform.

### class PointLightHelper extends LineSegments
A small octahedron wireframe at the point light's position.
- new PointLightHelper(light: PointLight, size: number, color: ColorInput | undefined)
- light: PointLight
- update(): void — Re-position the gizmo at the light and refresh its color.

### class Stats
A tiny performance overlay: frames-per-second and frame time (ms), with a rolling bar graph. Call {@link begin} at the start of your frame and {@link end} at the end (or just {@link update} once per frame). The timing math is decoupled from the DOM so it can be verified without a browser.
- new Stats(now: number)
- dom: HTMLDivElement | null — The overlay element (null when constructed without a `document`).
- historySize: 80 — Number of samples kept for the graph.
- fps: number — Most recent frames-per-second (updated about once a second).
- ms: number — Most recent measured frame time in milliseconds.
- begin(now?: number): void — Mark the start of a frame.
- end(now?: number): number — Mark the end of a frame; returns `now`.
- update(now?: number): void — Convenience: `end()` then `begin()` for the next frame.
- getHistory(): readonly number[] — Snapshot of recent per-second fps samples (oldest first).

### class Texture
A 2D texture backed by an ImageBitmap/canvas, uploaded lazily by the renderer.
- new Texture(source: TextureSource | null, options: TextureOptions)
- id: string
- isTexture: true
- name: string
- source: TextureSource | null
- wrapS: WrapMode
- wrapT: WrapMode
- magFilter: FilterMode
- minFilter: FilterMode
- generateMipmaps: boolean
- colorSpace: "linear" | "srgb"
- flipY: boolean
- version: number — Bumped to force re-upload.
- needsUpdate(): void

### class DataTexture extends Texture
A texture backed by raw pixel data (rather than an ImageBitmap). The renderer uploads `Float32Array` data as `rgba16float` (HDR environments) and `Uint8Array` data as `rgba8unorm`/`-srgb` (e.g. transcoded KTX2).
- new DataTexture(data: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>, width: number, height: number, options: TextureOptions)
- isDataTexture: true
- data: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike> — Interleaved RGBA data, length = width * height * 4.
- width: number
- height: number

### class CompressedDataTexture extends DataTexture
A GPU block-compressed texture (BC7 / ASTC 4×4 / ETC2). Uploaded directly to the GPU without a pixel-format conversion; no mipmap generation is performed.
- new CompressedDataTexture(blocks: Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>, width: number, height: number, gpuFormat: string, options: TextureOptions)
- isCompressedDataTexture: true
- gpuFormat: string — The WebGPU texture format (e.g.

### class ColorLUT
A 3-D color lookup table for display-space color grading, applied as the final post pass (after tonemap). `data` is `size³ × 3` RGB, red varying fastest — the layout of a `.cube` LUT and of a WebGPU 3-D texture (x = R, y = G, z = B).
- new ColorLUT(size: number, data: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>, strength: number)
- size: number
- data: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>
- domainMin: [number, number, number] — Input domain from `.cube` DOMAIN_MIN/MAX, per channel (default [0, 1]).
- domainMax: [number, number, number]
- strength: number — Blend toward the graded color in [0, 1] (1 = full grade).
- version: number — Bumped to force the post pipeline to re-upload the 3-D texture.

### class Light extends Object3D
Base light: a colored, intensity-scaled emitter in the scene graph.
- new Light(color: ColorInput | undefined, intensity: number)
- isLight: true
- color: Color
- intensity: number

### class AmbientLight extends Light
Uniform ambient fill applied equally to all surfaces.
- new AmbientLight(color: ColorInput | undefined, intensity: number)
- isAmbientLight: true

### class DirectionalLight extends Light
A light infinitely far away, casting parallel rays toward its target.
- new DirectionalLight(color: ColorInput | undefined, intensity: number)
- isDirectionalLight: true
- target: Object3D — Direction is from this object's world position toward the target.
- castShadow: boolean — When true and `renderer.shadows` is on, this light casts a shadow map.

### class PointLight extends Light
An omnidirectional light with physically-based inverse-square falloff.
- new PointLight(color: ColorInput | undefined, intensity: number, distance: number, decay: number)
- isPointLight: true
- distance: number — Maximum range of influence; 0 = infinite.
- decay: number — Additional falloff exponent (2 = physically correct).
- castShadow: boolean — Render this light's shadow into the cube-face shadow atlas (requires `renderer.shadows`).

### class SpotLight extends Light
A cone-shaped light with perspective falloff, angular attenuation, and optional shadow mapping. Direction is from this object's world position toward `target`.
- new SpotLight(color: ColorInput | undefined, intensity: number, distance: number, angle: number, penumbra: number, decay: number)
- isSpotLight: true
- angle: number — Half-angle of the light cone in radians (default = 60° full → PI/3 half).
- penumbra: number — Fraction of `angle` used for the penumbra (soft edge).
- distance: number — Maximum illumination range; 0 = infinite.
- decay: number — Falloff exponent (2 = physically correct inverse-square).
- castShadow: boolean — When true and `renderer.shadows` is on, this light writes a shadow map tile.
- target: Object3D — The spot aims from its world position toward this object.

### class WebGPURenderer
A WebGPU forward renderer with clustered-free multi-light PBR shading.
- new WebGPURenderer(options: RendererOptions)
- canvas: HTMLCanvasElement
- device: GPUDevice
- shadows: boolean — Enable directional shadow mapping for the first `castShadow` light.
- shadowMapSize: number — Shadow map resolution (square).
- shadowNormalBias: number — World-space normal offset applied before the depth comparison (reduces acne).
- shadowCascades: number — Number of directional shadow cascades.
- shadowCascadeLambda: number — Blend between logarithmic (1) and uniform (0) cascade split placement.
- shadowCascadeBlend: number — Fraction of each cascade depth range used to blend into the next cascade.
- volumetricFog: boolean — Integrate scene fog and clustered lights into a low-resolution 3-D froxel volume.
- postProcessing: boolean — Route rendering through the HDR post pipeline (tonemap moves to a final pass).
- fxaa: boolean — Apply FXAA in the post pipeline (only when `postProcessing` is on).
- bloom: boolean — Apply bloom in the post pipeline (only when `postProcessing` is on).
- bloomThreshold: number
- bloomIntensity: number
- toneMapping: ToneMapping — Output transform for the post pipeline: `'aces'` filmic (default), `'agx'` (AgX operator — gentler highlight desaturation), or `'none'` for sRGB-only output (flat/stylized looks).
- colorLUT: ColorLUT | null — Optional 3-D color-grading LUT applied as the final post pass (after tonemap, in display space).
- colorLift: Color — Display-space analytic grading applied before the optional 3-D LUT.
- colorGamma: Color
- colorGain: Color
- saturation: number
- autoExposure: boolean
- autoExposureMinEV: number
- autoExposureMaxEV: number
- autoExposureSpeed: number
- vignette: number
- chromaticAberration: number
- bloomStreak: number
- lensFlare: number
- passes: ShaderPass[] — Custom fullscreen post effects, run in order in HDR linear space before tonemap (requires `postProcessing`).
- oit: boolean — Order-independent transparency (weighted-blended).
- ssao: boolean — Screen-space ambient occlusion.
- ssaoRadius: number
- ssaoBias: number
- ssaoStrength: number
- ssr: boolean — Screen-space reflections.
- ssrIntensity: number — Strength of the reflected HDR contribution.
- ssrMaxDistance: number — Maximum view-space ray length in world units.
- ssrThickness: number — View-space hit tolerance in world units.
- taa: boolean — Temporal anti-aliasing: a sub-pixel Halton jitter is baked into the projection matrix and a resolve pass blends the reprojected history (camera-motion only).
- taaBlend: number — TAA blend factor: weight of the current frame (lower = smoother, more ghosting).
- motionBlur: boolean — Per-object reconstruction motion blur.
- motionBlurStrength: number
- depthOfField: boolean — Depth-aware HDR bokeh blur.
- focusDistance: number
- aperture: number
- maxBlur: number
- deterministic: boolean — Deterministic rendering: identical scenes produce identical pixels.
- time: number — Scene time in seconds; only advances when you set it (`deterministic = true`).
- renderBundles: boolean — Record the opaque draws into a render bundle to amortize encoding cost.
- gpuCulling: boolean — GPU-driven frustum culling: a compute shader tests bounding spheres against the camera frustum and writes instanceCount 0/1 into an indirect draw buffer.
- occlusionCulling: boolean — Hi-Z occlusion culling (opt-in, builds on `gpuCulling`).
- clusteredLighting: boolean — Clustered forward+ lighting: a compute shader bins light bounding spheres into a 16×9×24 screen-tile/depth-slice grid each frame; fragments shade only the lights in their cluster (up to 32), so hundreds of ranged lights stay cheap.
- onDeviceLost: ((info: GPUDeviceLostInfo) => void) | undefined — Called when the GPU device is lost unexpectedly; call `restoreContext()` to recover.
- frustumCulling: boolean — Skip meshes whose bounding sphere is outside the camera frustum.
- culledCount: number — Number of meshes culled in the last frame (diagnostics).
- init(): Promise<void>
- restoreContext(): Promise<void> — Rebuild after a lost device (or to recover from a GPU reset).
- dispose(): void — Release GPU resources and destroy the device.
- isDisposed: boolean — True once `dispose()` has run.
- isDeviceLost: boolean — True while the device is lost and not yet restored.
- resources(): { textureMemoryBytes: number; spriteBatches: number; fontAtlases: number; modelPoolSlots: number; } — Debug snapshot of tracked GPU resource usage — for spotting leaks in long-running sessions.
- setPixelRatio(ratio: number): void
- setSize(width: number, height: number): void — Resize backing store.
- drawingBufferWidth: number
- drawingBufferHeight: number
- render(scene: Scene, camera: Camera, target?: RenderTarget | undefined): void
- report(): RenderReport — Last-frame statistics as plain JSON: draw calls, triangles, culling results, memory estimates, and active feature flags.
- diagnose(scene: Scene, camera: Camera): Diagnostic[] — Explain why a scene "renders but looks wrong" — especially black screens.
- readPixels(target?: RenderTarget | undefined): Promise<PixelData> — Read back rendered pixels as RGBA8 (rows top-to-bottom).
- screenshot(target?: RenderTarget | undefined): Promise<Blob> — Capture a PNG of the next canvas frame (or of a RenderTarget).
- bakeIrradianceProbes(grid: IrradianceProbeGrid, scene: Scene, options?: IrradianceBakeOptions): Promise<Float32Array<ArrayBuffer>> — Capture and GPU-project every point in an irradiance grid to SH-L2.
- exposure: number
- pickAt(cssX: number, cssY: number, scene: Scene, camera: Camera): Promise<Mesh | null> — Render an offscreen id-buffer pass and read back the pixel at (cssX, cssY) to identify which mesh lies under the cursor.

### class FrameMismatchError extends Error
Thrown by `expectFrame` on mismatch; carries inspectable artifacts.
- new FrameMismatchError(message: string, result: CompareResult, actual: PixelData, actualPNG: Blob, diffPNG: Blob)
- result: CompareResult
- actual: PixelData — The frame that was actually rendered (save it to update the golden).
- actualPNG: Blob — PNG of the rendered frame.
- diffPNG: Blob — PNG visualizing the differences in red.

### class OrbitControls
Mouse/touch orbit-pan-zoom camera controls with inertial damping.
- new OrbitControls(camera: PerspectiveCamera, domElement: HTMLElement)
- enabled: boolean
- target: Vector3
- minDistance: number
- maxDistance: number
- minPolarAngle: number
- maxPolarAngle: number
- enableDamping: boolean
- dampingFactor: number
- rotateSpeed: number
- zoomSpeed: number
- panSpeed: number
- autoRotate: boolean
- autoRotateSpeed: number
- dispose(): void
- setTarget(center: Vector3, distance?: number | undefined): void — Frame an object/bounds: position the target at center and back off to fit.
- update(): boolean

### class FlyControls
First-person / fly camera controls. WASD strafes in the camera plane, Q/E (or Space/Ctrl) move along the world up axis, and the mouse looks around — drag by default, or grab the pointer with {@link lock} for a true free-look.
- new FlyControls(camera: Camera, domElement: HTMLElement)
- enabled: boolean
- movementSpeed: number — World units per second.
- lookSpeed: number — Radians of rotation per pixel of mouse motion.
- boostFactor: number — Multiplier applied while a boost key (Shift) is held.
- maxPolarAngle: number — Clamp pitch to just under straight up/down to avoid gimbal flip.
- verticalIsWorldUp: boolean — When true, vertical motion follows world up; when false, the camera's own up.
- dispose(): void
- lock(): void — Request pointer lock for continuous free-look (no dragging needed).
- unlock(): void — Release a pointer lock acquired via {@link lock}.
- update(delta: number): void — Integrate one frame of movement/rotation.

### class GLTFLoader
Loads glTF 2.0 (.gltf + .bin + images) and binary glTF (.glb). Supports node hierarchy, meshes/primitives, PBR metallic-roughness materials, textures/samplers, skinning, morph targets, keyframe animation (translation/rotation/scale/weights), and KHR_materials_emissive_strength.
- setMeshoptDecoder(decoder: MeshoptDecoder): GLTFLoader — Provide a meshoptimizer decoder to enable `EXT_meshopt_compression`.
- setKTX2Loader(loader: KTX2TextureLoader): GLTFLoader — Provide a KTX2 loader/transcoder to enable `KHR_texture_basisu`.
- setDracoDecoder(decoder: DracoDecoder): GLTFLoader — Provide a Draco decoder to enable `KHR_draco_mesh_compression`.
- load(url: string): Promise<GLTFResult> — Load from a URL (resolves relative buffers/images against it).
- parse(data: ArrayBuffer, baseUrl?: string): Promise<GLTFResult> — Parse an ArrayBuffer that is either a .glb or a UTF-8 .gltf JSON.
- buildFromPreloaded(json: GLTFRoot, buffers: ArrayBuffer[], images: (ImageBitmap | null)[]): Promise<GLTFResult> — Build a {@link GLTFResult} from pre-loaded resources (used by {@link WorkerGLTFLoader }).

### class WorkerGLTFLoader
A drop-in replacement for {@link GLTFLoader} that performs the I/O-heavy work (buffer fetching, image decoding via `createImageBitmap`) in a Web Worker, keeping the main thread free during loads. The final scene-graph construction (geometry, materials, Object3D hierarchy) still runs on the main thread.
- setMeshoptDecoder(decoder: MeshoptDecoder): WorkerGLTFLoader
- setDracoDecoder(decoder: DracoDecoder): WorkerGLTFLoader
- setKTX2Loader(loader: KTX2TextureLoader): WorkerGLTFLoader
- load(url: string): Promise<GLTFResult>
- terminate(): void

### class RGBELoader
Loads Radiance `.hdr` (RGBE) equirectangular environment maps into a float {@link DataTexture}, suitable for `scene.environment`. Supports the new-format RLE scanlines and the flat/old fallback.
- load(url: string, options?: TextureOptions | undefined): Promise<DataTexture>
- parse(buffer: ArrayBuffer, options?: TextureOptions): DataTexture — Parse `.hdr` bytes into an RGBA Float32 {@link DataTexture}.

### class KTX2Loader
Loads KTX2 textures (for `KHR_texture_basisu`). Uncompressed RGBA8 payloads are uploaded directly; Basis-supercompressed payloads need a transcoder ({@link setTranscoder}) that yields RGBA8. When a GPUDevice is registered via {@link setDevice} and the transcoder implements `transcodeToCompressed`, the loader will transcode to BC7/ASTC/ETC2 (whichever the device prefers) instead of RGBA8.
- setTranscoder(transcoder: BasisTranscoder): KTX2Loader
- setDevice(device: GPUDevice): KTX2Loader — Provide the WebGPU device so the loader can query feature support and upload compressed textures using the preferred native format.
- load(url: string, options?: TextureOptions | undefined): Promise<Texture>
- parse(data: Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>, srgb?: boolean, options?: TextureOptions): Promise<Texture> — Parse + (if needed) transcode KTX2 bytes into a `DataTexture`.

### class GLTFExporter
Exports a scene-graph subtree to glTF 2.0 (binary `.glb`). Covers the round-trippable core: node hierarchy + TRS, mesh geometry (position / normal / uv / color / indices), `StandardMaterial` PBR factors + textures, clearcoat / ior / specular / sheen extensions, morph targets, skinning, and animations. All public methods are async to support texture encoding.
- parse(root: Object3D, animations?: AnimationClip[]): Promise<GLTFExportResult>
- parseGLB(root: Object3D, animations?: AnimationClip[]): Promise<ArrayBuffer> — Convenience: export just the `.glb` ArrayBuffer.
- parseGLTF(root: Object3D, animations?: AnimationClip[]): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> — Export to a standalone `.gltf` JSON object with the binary embedded as a base64 data-URI buffer (re-loadable directly by `GLTFLoader`).

### class SceneSerializer
vela's native scene format: a compact, lossless-enough JSON round-trip for the scene graph — `Object3D`/`Mesh`/`LineSegments`/lights/irradiance grids, their transforms, `BufferGeometry` attributes, and `StandardMaterial`/`LineBasicMaterial`. Geometries and materials are de-duplicated into shared tables. (Textures, skinning, morphs, and animation are not serialized.)

### class AnimationClip
A named set of keyframe tracks with a shared duration.
- new AnimationClip(name: string, tracks: KeyframeTrack[], duration: number | undefined)
- name: string
- tracks: KeyframeTrack[]
- duration: number
- events: AnimationEvent[] — Sorted timeline markers (footstep, hit-frame, …) fired by the mixer.
- addEvent(time: number, name: string): AnimationClip — Add a timeline marker at `time` seconds; events stay sorted by time.

### class AnimationMixer
Plays and blends `AnimationClip`s. Each clip runs as an `AnimationAction` with its own time/weight; the mixer samples every enabled action and blends the results per (node, path) by weight — weighted average for translation/ scale/morph weights, normalized weighted sum (nlerp) for rotation. Bindings are cached, so a steady action set costs no per-frame allocation.
- actions: AnimationAction[]
- timeScale: number — Global speed multiplier applied on top of each action's `timeScale`.
- paused: boolean
- loop: boolean — Default loop mode applied to actions created by `play`.
- play(clip: AnimationClip): AnimationMixer — Play `clip` exclusively at full weight (replaces any current actions).
- add(clip: AnimationClip, weight?: number): AnimationAction — Add another clip as an action (for blending); returns it for tuning.
- crossFadeTo(clip: AnimationClip, duration: number): AnimationAction — Cross-fade to `clip` over `duration` seconds: the new action fades in from 0→1 while every currently-enabled action fades out to 0 (and is pruned once gone).
- stop(): AnimationMixer
- clip: AnimationClip | null — The primary (first) action's clip, or null — for single-clip callers.
- time: number — The primary (first) action's time, or 0.
- setTime(t: number): AnimationMixer — Jump every action to absolute time `t` (seconds) and re-blend.
- update(dt: number): void — Advance all actions by `dt` seconds, then blend them into the targets.

### class AnimationAction
One playing instance of an `AnimationClip` inside an `AnimationMixer`: its own playback time, weight, and (optional) per-bone mask. The mixer blends all enabled actions by weight each frame. Drive playback through the mixer; tweak `weight` / `timeScale` / `loop` directly, or use `fadeTo` for ramps.
- new AnimationAction(clip: AnimationClip)
- clip: AnimationClip
- weight: number — Blend weight; the mixer normalizes across enabled actions.
- time: number — Playback time in seconds.
- timeScale: number — Per-action speed multiplier (combined with the mixer's `timeScale`).
- loop: boolean
- paused: boolean
- enabled: boolean — Disabled actions are skipped by the blend and pruned once faded to 0.
- additive: boolean — Additive layer: instead of averaging into the base pose, add this clip's delta from `referenceTime` on top of it (e.g.
- referenceTime: number — Pose subtracted to form the additive delta (the clip's rest frame).
- mask: Set<Object3D> | null — When set, only tracks targeting a node in this set contribute — a per-bone mask (e.g.
- onEvent: ((name: string, time: number) => void) | null — Fired by the mixer when playback crosses one of the clip's `events` (loop-aware).
- setMask(targets: Object3D[] | null): AnimationAction — Restrict this action to the given target nodes (per-bone mask).
- fadeTo(target: number, duration: number): AnimationAction — Ramp `weight` toward `target` over `duration` seconds (0 = instant).
- fadeIn(duration: number): AnimationAction
- fadeOut(duration: number): AnimationAction
- advanceFade(dt: number): boolean — Advance any active weight ramp by `dt`; returns true while still fading.

### class AnimationStateMachine
A declarative animation state machine over an `AnimationMixer`. States are single clips or 1-D blend spaces; transitions fire on parameter conditions and crossfade. Each frame it sets the mixer's per-clip action weights, so all the blending/cross-fade machinery is reused. Introspect with `describe()`.
- new AnimationStateMachine(def: StateMachineDef)
- mixer: AnimationMixer
- parameters: Record<string, number>
- current: string
- setParameter(name: string, value: number): AnimationStateMachine
- play(name: string, duration?: number): AnimationStateMachine — Immediately switch to `name` with an optional crossfade (no condition check).
- update(dt: number): void — Evaluate transitions, accumulate state weights into the mixer, and advance it.
- describe(): { current: string; parameters: Record<string, number>; transition: { from: string; to: string; progress: number; } | null; active: { clip: string; weight: number; }[]; } — JSON-friendly snapshot: current state, parameters, transition, active clips.

### class KeyframeTrack
A single animated channel: keyframe `times` driving one transform `path` (translation/scale = vec3, rotation = quaternion) of a target node.
- new KeyframeTrack(target: Object3D, path: TrackPath, times: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>, values: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>, interpolation: InterpolationMode, valueSize: number | undefined)
- target: Object3D
- path: TrackPath
- times: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>
- values: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>
- interpolation: InterpolationMode
- stride: number — Components per value: 3 for translation/scale, 4 for rotation, or the morph-target count for weights (supplied via `valueSize`).
- duration: number
- sample(time: number): void — Evaluate at `time` and write the result into the target transform.
- evaluate(time: number, out: Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>): void — Evaluate at `time` into `out` (length ≥ `stride`) as raw components — translation/scale = xyz, rotation = xyzw (unit), weights = per-target — without touching the target node.

- fromArray(a: ArrayLike<number>, offset?: number): Vector2

- cross(v: Vector3): Vector3

### class Matrix4

- makeOrthographic(left: number, right: number, top: number, bottom: number, near: number, far: number): Matrix4 — Right-handed orthographic projection mapping z to [0, 1] (WebGPU NDC).

### class Box3

### class Plane
A plane in Hessian normal form: normal·x + constant = 0.
- new Plane(normal: Vector3, constant: number)
- normal: Vector3
- constant: number
- set(nx: number, ny: number, nz: number, constant: number): Plane
- normalize(): Plane — Scale so the normal is unit length (keeps distances metric).

### class Sphere
A bounding sphere.
- new Sphere(center: Vector3, radius: number)
- center: Vector3
- radius: number
- set(center: Vector3, radius: number): Sphere
- copy(s: Sphere): Sphere
- clone(): Sphere
- isEmpty(): boolean
- applyMatrix4(m: Matrix4): Sphere — Transform center by the matrix and scale radius by its max axis scale.

### class Frustum
A view frustum as six inward-facing planes, extracted from a view-projection matrix (Gribb-Hartmann) for WebGPU's [0, 1] clip depth.
- planes: [Plane, Plane, Plane, Plane, Plane, Plane]
- setFromProjectionMatrix(m: Matrix4): Frustum — Build from m = projection * view.
- intersectsSphere(sphere: Sphere): boolean
- intersectsBox(box: Box3): boolean

### class Ray
A ray with an origin and a normalized direction.
- new Ray(origin: Vector3, direction: Vector3)
- origin: Vector3
- direction: Vector3
- set(origin: Vector3, direction: Vector3): Ray
- copy(ray: Ray): Ray
- at(t: number, target: Vector3): Vector3
- intersectSphere(sphere: Sphere): number | null — Distance along the ray to the first sphere intersection, or null.
- intersectBox(box: Box3): number | null — Distance along the ray to the first AABB intersection, or null.
- intersectTriangle(a: Vector3, b: Vector3, c: Vector3, backfaceCulling: boolean, target?: Vector3 | undefined): number | null — Distance along the ray to a triangle intersection, or null.
- applyMatrix4(m: Matrix4): Ray — Transform the ray by a matrix (origin as a point, direction as a vector).

## Functions

### function storage(opts?: Omit<StorageBinding, "kind">): StorageBinding
`storage({...})` / `uniform({...})` helpers for `ComputeTask` bindings.

### function uniform(values: Record<string, UniformValue>): UniformBinding


### function gradientTexture(stops: GradientStop[], width?: number): DataTexture
Build a 1-D gradient as a `width × 1` linear `DataTexture` (clamp-wrapped, linearly filtered) — the generic primitive behind toon ramps, gradient maps, and color LUTs. Stops take `ColorInput` (a `Color` or linear `[r, g, b]`), so there is no hidden color space. Plug it into a `ShaderMaterial`/`ShaderPass` texture uniform and sample it at `(t, 0.5)`:

### function computeCascadeSplits(near: number, far: number, count: number, lambda?: number, out?: Float32Array<ArrayBuffer>): Float32Array<ArrayBufferLike>
Practical CSM split scheme: lambda=0 uniform, lambda=1 logarithmic.

### function diagnoseScene(scene: Scene, camera: Camera, state: DiagnoseState): Diagnostic[]
Triage why a scene "renders but looks wrong" — especially the classic black screen. Pure scene-graph math: runs without a GPU. Returns an empty array when nothing looks suspicious.

### function describeScene(scene: Scene, camera?: Camera | undefined): SceneDescription
Summarize a scene as plain JSON an agent can read: node/light/material inventories, world bounds, environment/fog state, named nodes, and (with a camera) per-mesh frustum visibility. Pure scene-graph math — no GPU.

### function captureFrame(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Scene, camera: Camera, options?: CaptureOptions): Promise<PixelData>
Render deterministically and capture the final post-processed canvas frame.

### function comparePixels(actual: PixelData, expected: PixelData, options?: CompareOptions): CompareResult
Pure pixel comparison (usable offline / in node).

### function loadPixels(source: string | Blob): Promise<PixelData>
Decode a PNG/JPEG URL (or Blob) into pixels. Browser-only.

### function pixelsToPNG(pixels: PixelData): Promise<Blob>
Encode pixels as a PNG Blob. Browser-only.

### function expectFrame(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Scene, camera: Camera, golden: string | PixelData | Blob, options?: CaptureOptions & CompareOptions): Promise<CompareResult>
Render deterministically and assert the frame matches a golden image. On mismatch, throws `FrameMismatchError` with metrics plus the actual and diff frames as PNG blobs (also logged as object URLs for quick viewing).

### function solveTwoBoneIK(root: Object3D, mid: Object3D, end: Object3D, target: Vector3, options?: TwoBoneIKOptions): void
Analytic two-bone IK: rotate `root` and `mid` (local quaternions) so `end` reaches `target` (world space), with the joint bending toward an optional `pole`. `mid` must be a child of `root` and `end` a descendant of `mid`.

### function clamp(value: number, min: number, max: number): number


### function lerp(a: number, b: number, t: number): number


### function degToRad(deg: number): number


### function radToDeg(rad: number): number


### function generateUUID(): string


## Interfaces & types

### Intersection
```ts
export interface Intersection {
  object: Mesh;
  distance: number;
  point: Vector3;
  faceIndex?: number;
  uv?: Vector2;
}
```

### SkyOptions
Procedural daylight sky (Preetham analytic model).
```ts
export interface SkyOptions {
  sunDirection: Vector3;
  turbidity?: number;
}
```

### FogOptions
Distance fog. Provide `density` for exponential-squared fog, or `near`/`far` for linear fog (density takes precedence when both are set).
```ts
export interface FogOptions {
  color: Color;
  near?: number;
  far?: number;
  density?: number;
  heightFalloff?: number;
}
```

### Shell
Inverted-hull shell pass for a mesh: after the mesh draws, the same geometry is drawn again with back faces (front-culled), extruded `thickness` world units along the vertex normal, using `material`. This is the generic draw primitive behind outline shells, fur, and selection highlights — the look (flat color, fresnel, fur texture, …) lives in `material` (any `StandardMaterial`/`ShaderMaterial`); the engine only provides the extruded back-face draw. Not supported on `InstancedMesh`.
```ts
export interface Shell {
  material: Material;
  thickness: number;
}
```

### ParticleSystemOptions
Declarative GPU particle emitter config. All fields are plain values — mutate them freely; the renderer re-reads them every frame (no flags). `[start, end]` pairs interpolate linearly over each particle's life.
```ts
export interface ParticleSystemOptions {
  capacity?: number;
  rate?: number;
  lifetime?: number | [number, number];
  velocity?: Vector3;
  spread?: number;
  gravity?: Vector3;
  size?: number | [number, number];
  color?: Color | [Color, Color];
  opacity?: number | [number, number];
  blending?: 'additive' | 'alpha';
}
```

### TrailOptions
```ts
export interface TrailOptions {
  material?: Material;
  maxPoints?: number;
  width?: number;
  widthTail?: number;
  minDistance?: number;
}
```

```ts
export interface TextMeshOptions {
```

### StorageBinding
A storage buffer binding: either a byte size, or initial data to upload.

```ts
export interface StorageBinding {
```

### Diagnostic
One finding from `renderer.diagnose()`: machine-matchable and human-fixable.
```ts
export interface Diagnostic {
  severity: 'error' | 'warning';
  code: string;
  message: string;
  fix: string;
}
```

### DiagnoseState
Renderer state snapshot the checks need (kept GPU-free for offline testing).
```ts
export interface DiagnoseState {
  postProcessing: boolean;

  oit: boolean;
  ssao: boolean;
  ssr: boolean;
  taa: boolean;
  shadows: boolean;
  shadowCascades?: number;
  volumetricFog?: boolean;
  motionBlur?: boolean;
  depthOfField?: boolean;
  canvasWidth: number;
  canvasHeight: number;
}
```

### SceneDescription
```ts
export interface SceneDescription {
  counts: {
    nodes: number;

    particleSystems: number;
    sprites: number;
    texts: number;

    lights: Record<string, number>;
  };
  bounds: { center: [number, number, number]; size: [number, number, number]; radius: number } | null;
  materials: Array<{ type: string; name: string; users: number; transparent: boolean }>;
  environment: 'texture' | 'procedural-sky' | 'none';
  skybox: boolean;
  fog: 'linear' | 'exp2' | 'none';
  named: Array<{ name: string; type: string; position: [number, number, number]; inFrustum?: boolean }>;
  visibility?: { meshesTested: number; inFrustum: number; outOfFrustum: number };
}
```

### RenderReport
Last-frame statistics from `renderer.report()` — JSON an agent can reason over.
```ts
export interface RenderReport {
  frame: number;
  drawCalls: number;
  triangles: number;
  meshes: { opaque: number; transparent: number; culled: number };
  lights: number;
  particles: { systems: number; poolCapacity: number };
  sprites: { batches: number; instances: number };
  shadowDraws: number;
  textureMemoryBytes: number;
  flags: { postProcessing: boolean; clusteredLighting: boolean; ssr: boolean; msaa: number; shadows: boolean; volumetricFog: boolean; motionBlur: boolean };
  suggestions: PerfSuggestion[];
}
```

### PerfSuggestion
An actionable performance suggestion (same shape as a Diagnostic).
```ts
export interface PerfSuggestion {
  code: string;
  message: string;
  fix: string;
}
```

### CaptureOptions
Golden-image testing helpers: render deterministically, read pixels back, and compare against a reference with actionable failure artifacts. Built for agents — a visual change becomes a runnable assertion.
```ts
export interface CaptureOptions {
  frames?: number;
  timeStep?: number;
  startTime?: number;
}
```

```ts
export interface CompareOptions {

}
```

```ts
export interface CompareResult {

  maxDelta: number;

}
```

```ts
export interface GLTFResult {

}
```

### BasisTranscoder
Transcodes a Basis-supercompressed KTX2 payload to RGBA8. Wrap the standard Basis/KTX2 transcoder (which can transcode to `RGBA32`) and plug it in via {@link KTX2Loader.setTranscoder}.
```ts
export interface BasisTranscoder {
  ready?: Promise<void>;
  transcodeToRGBA(ktx2: Uint8Array): KTX2Image | Promise<KTX2Image>;
  transcodeToCompressed?(
    ktx2: Uint8Array,
    format: 'bc7-rgba-unorm' | 'astc-4x4-unorm' | 'etc2-rgba8unorm',
  ): CompressedKTX2Image | Promise<CompressedKTX2Image>;
}
```

### KTX2Image
A decoded KTX2 level: tightly-packed RGBA8 pixels.
```ts
export interface KTX2Image {
  width: number;
  height: number;
  rgba: Uint8Array;
}
```

### MeshoptDecoder
The subset of meshoptimizer's `MeshoptDecoder` that vela uses for `EXT_meshopt_compression`. Pass the standard module:
```ts
export interface MeshoptDecoder {
  ready: Promise<void>;
  decodeGltfBuffer(
    target: Uint8Array,
    count: number,
    size: number,
    source: Uint8Array,
    mode: string,
    filter?: string,
  ): void;
}
```

### KTX2TextureLoader
Transcodes a KTX2 payload into a renderable {@link Texture} (used for `KHR_texture_basisu`). {@link KTX2Loader } implements this; Basis-supercompressed payloads need a transcoder plugged into it.
```ts
export interface KTX2TextureLoader {
  parse(data: Uint8Array, srgb: boolean): Texture | Promise<Texture>;
}
```

### DracoDecoder
Minimal interface for a Draco mesh decoder (for `KHR_draco_mesh_compression`). Implement against the `draco3d` or `draco3dgltf` WASM module and pass an instance via {@link GLTFLoader.setDracoDecoder }.
```ts
export interface DracoDecoder {
  ready?: Promise<void>;
  decode(data: Uint8Array, attributeIds: Record<string, number>): DracoGeometry | Promise<DracoGeometry>;
}
```

### DracoGeometry
Decoded geometry from a Draco-compressed mesh primitive. The `attributes` map contains per-attribute typed arrays (Float32Array for float attributes, Uint32Array for integer attributes such as JOINTS_0).
```ts
export interface DracoGeometry {
  indices: Uint32Array;
  attributes: Record<string, { array: Float32Array | Uint32Array; itemSize: number }>;
}
```

### GLTFExportResult
Result of an export: the glTF JSON plus the packed binary (a `.glb`).
```ts
export interface GLTFExportResult {
  json: Record<string, unknown>;
  glb: ArrayBuffer;
}
```

### AnimationEvent
A timeline marker on a clip; the mixer fires it when playback crosses `time`.
```ts
export interface AnimationEvent {
  time: number;
  name: string;
}
```

### TwoBoneIKOptions
```ts
export interface TwoBoneIKOptions {
  pole?: Vector3;
}
```

### StateMachineDef
```ts
export interface StateMachineDef {
  states: StateDef[];
  transitions: TransitionDef[];
  initial?: string;
  parameters?: Record<string, number>;
}
```

### StateDef
A graph node: either a single `clip`, or a 1-D `blend` space that mixes its samples by the value of `parameter` (nearest two, linearly weighted).
```ts
export interface StateDef {
  name: string;
  clip?: AnimationClip;
  blend?: { parameter: string; samples: BlendSample[] };
}
```

### TransitionDef
`from → to` when every condition in `when` holds; `from: '*'` matches any state.
```ts
export interface TransitionDef {
  from: string;
  to: string;
  when: Condition[];
  duration?: number;
}
```

### Condition
A comparison on a named parameter; a transition fires when all of its conditions hold.
```ts
export interface Condition {
  parameter: string;
  op: '<' | '<=' | '>' | '>=' | '==' | '!=';
  value: number;
}
```

### BlendSample
A 1-D blend-space sample: a clip placed at `position` along the blend parameter.
```ts
export interface BlendSample {
  clip: AnimationClip;
  position: number;
}
```

### InterpolationMode
```ts
export type InterpolationMode = 'STEP' | 'LINEAR' | 'CUBICSPLINE';
```

### TrackPath
```ts
export type TrackPath = 'translation' | 'rotation' | 'scale' | 'weights';
```

### EulerOrder
```ts
export type EulerOrder = 'XYZ' | 'YXZ' | 'ZXY' | 'ZYX' | 'YZX' | 'XZY';
```

### ColorInput
Anything accepted where a color is expected: a {@link Color}, or a linear `[r, g, b]` (optionally `[r, g, b, a]`) array. Packed `0xRRGGBB` hex is deliberately not accepted — use `new Color().setHex(...)` to opt into sRGB hex.
```ts
export type ColorInput = Color | readonly number[];
```
